chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Safwan al-Jus, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The believer is the one when he is angry, his anger does not lead him out of truth, and when he is pleased, his pleasure does not lead him into falsehood, and when he has power, he does not take more than what is for him.'
ai.seo_question: What are the defining signs of a true believer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) outlines the spiritual equilibrium of the true believer, ensuring that emotional volatility in anger and joy does not distort judgment or lead to excess. This triad of self-mastery—maintaining truth in wrath, avoiding falsehood in delight, and practicing moderation in capacity—reflects the Shia ideal of the 'balanced soul' (al-nafs al-mutma'inna). The narration serves as a practical guide for ethical conduct, linking internal emotional regulation to external justice and restraint.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Safwan Al Jammal who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘But rather, the Momin is the one when he is angry, his anger does not exit him from a truth, and when is please, his pleasure does not enter him into a falsehood, and when he is able, he does not take any more than what is for him’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from Safwan al-Jammal who has said the following: “

Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Of believers are only those who even on becoming angry do not deviate from the truth and when they become happy it does not take them into falsehood and when in power they do not take more than what is for them.’”
